title: Stop Focusing On Negative Emotions | English & Chill with Jennie | English Podcast

transcript.text: Hi, my dear friends.
It's Jenny here.
How are you really feeling today?
Some days feel light.
Like the world is on your side and everything moves with ease.
But other days, things feel heavier.
You wake up and the air around you already feels thick.
Like there's a weight sitting quietly on your chest.
Not because of the weather, but because of the emotions you carry.
Maybe it's worry, maybe it's exhaustion, or maybe it's the quiet ache of trying so hard
for so long, without anyone really noticing.
If that's you today, I want you to know you're not alone.
You don't always have to be strong, or cheerful, or full of energy.
Sometimes just making it through the day is already enough.
So tell me, how has your day been?
Was it gentle?
Or did it ask a lot from your heart?
Have you ever felt like a heavy cloud was sitting on your chest?
Not because of the weather, but because of the emotions you carry?
We all have days like that.
Sometimes it's not one big event.
It's not one dramatic heartbreak.
It's just the small, sharp pieces of frustration, disappointment, or sadness that slowly
collect inside us.
And the truth is, those little pieces add weight.
They change how we see the world.
You wake up in the morning and notice what went wrong yesterday before you notice the sun
outside your window.
You hear one negative comment, and it sounds louder than ten kind words.
You try to move forward, but your attention keeps circling back to what hurt you.
It's like carrying a bag that keeps getting heavier.
At first you think, it's fine, I can hold this.
But as the hours, weeks, and months go by, the bag doesn't feel light anymore.
It feels impossible.
I want you to pause for a moment here.
Think about how you've been carrying your own bag of emotions.
What's inside it?
Maybe stress from work, maybe loneliness, maybe the memory of someone's careless words.
You might not even notice how much it affects your steps.
But deep down, you feel it.
Here's something important.
When we focus on our negative emotions, we're not just feeling them, we're feeding them.
Imagine watering a plant every single day.
If the plant is joy, it grows strong and green.
But if the plant is bitterness, it grows too.
And soon it takes up all the space.
This is what happens inside us.
What we focus on, expands.
I don't want you to hear me wrong.
This isn't about ignoring pain or pretending everything is fine.
Negative emotions are part of being human.
They are signals, like road signs.
They tell us, you need rest, you need healing, you need change.
But here's the trap.
If we hold those signs in our hands forever, if we keep staring at them, we never move forward.
Maybe right now you're carrying anger from something unfair.
Maybe you're carrying regret from a choice you can't undo.
Maybe you're carrying sadness because life feels harder than it should.
And you know what?
It's okay to admit that.
It's okay to feel that.
But I want you to imagine what it would feel like.
To put down that heavy bag, even for just one moment, your shoulders would relax.
Your breath would deepen.
Your eyes would finally see more than the weight.
The reason I'm talking about this is simple.
When you practice English with me, you're not just learning words.
You're also learning how to notice.
Noticing feelings, noticing patterns, noticing the way your mind moves.
And when you become aware of how often you feed your negative emotions, you can also choose
not to.
That choice is powerful.
Quite.
But it changes everything.
Before we move deeper, let me ask you this.
What would your day look like if you focused less on what went wrong and more on what was
still good?
Would your steps feel lighter?
Would your heart feel freer?
So today we begin with this simple truth.
Negative emotions are real, but we don't have to let them shape our whole world.
You have the power to notice the weight you carry.
And slowly, gently, learn how to put some of it down.
Have you ever wondered why your mind remembers painful words longer than kind ones?
Think about it.
One compliment may feel nice for a few hours, but one insult can echo for years.
It's almost unfair, isn't it?
The reason lies in how our brain is built.
Survival depended on noticing danger quickly.
If our ancestors ignored the rustle of a wild animal, they could lose their life.
But if they ignored the sound of birds singing, nothing dangerous happened.
So over time, the brain learned.
Negative equals important.
Negative equals urgent.
And that old wiring is still inside us today.
And if we're safe in our homes, our mind reacts to stress like it's life or death.
This explains why a bad memory feels heavier than a good one.
Why one mistake at work can ruin your whole day, even if nine things went right.
Why your heart beats faster when you read criticism, but not when you hear quiet praise.
Your brain believes that holding onto pain will protect you.
It thinks, if I never forget, I will never be hurt again.
But here's the truth.
Holding on doesn't protect you.
It only keeps the wound open.
Let me share something I've noticed in my own life.
Sometimes after teaching, I receive messages from people saying, Jenny, thank you.
Your podcast helped me.
Those words make me smile.
But if one message says, your voice is boring, guess which one my brain repeats.
It's not because the negative voice is louder.
It's because my mind gives it more weight.
It's almost like pain sticks to us while joy slips away.
I want you to think about your own experiences.
Can you remember a moment when one negative comment stayed with you for days?
Maybe it was a teacher, a friend, or even a stranger online?
Now compare that to the kind things people have said.
Do you remember them as clearly?
Or do they feel softer?
More distant.
This is the unfair game our brain plays.
It clings to pain because it thinks pain is safer to a remember.
But here's where the surprise comes in.
You can teach your mind a new habit.
You can gently remind yourself, I don't need to keep this forever.
I can let this pass through me.
It doesn't mean the pain was not real.
It means you choose not to let it take all the space.
Imagine your thoughts like a small village.
In this village, every thought is a traveler.
Some bring gifts of joy, peace, and laughter.
Others bring heavy bags of anger and fear.
If you only open the doors to negative travelers, the village becomes dark.
But if you also welcome the positive ones, the light returns.
The key is not letting one difficult traveler take over every house.
So here's a gentle reminder.
Your brain may cling to pain, but you are not your brain.
You are the one who chooses where to place your attention.
Maybe you just needed someone to say, it's okay.
It's okay if you've been caring too much.
It's okay if you've been replaying the same hurt in your head.
Because noticing this pattern is the first step to freedom, take a slow breath right now.
Feel the air move in.
Feel it move out.
This is proof.
You are here in this moment, not in the past, not in the memory.
You don't need to live inside the echo of old pain.
So as we continue, keep this picture in mind.
The brain will cling to pain.
But the heart always knows how to find light again if we let it.
If the mind naturally clings to pain, how do we shift?
How do we move our focus from what hurts to what heals?
The answer is not enforcing yourself to be positive.
It's in noticing small joys.
It's in celebrating simple wins.
Think of it like turning your head.
If you only look to the left, you see one view.
But if you gently turn to the right, a whole different world appears.
The world didn't change.
Your attention did.
This is what happens with emotions.
What you look at becomes larger.
So if you choose again and again to notice something kind, something gentle, something hopeful,
that becomes your new view.
Let me give you an example.
Imagine you're walking home after a long difficult day.
Your boss was unfair.
The traffic was terrible.
The heat was heavy.
Your mind starts to repeat, why is everything so hard?
Why does this always happen to me?
But then, you notice a child laughing as she chases a balloon.
You notice the way the sky glows, soft pink at sunset.
You notice the cool drink waiting on your kitchen table.
The problems are still there.
But your heart feels different because you allowed a new focus to enter.
As people think, joy has to be big, a dream vacation, a new car, a perfect relationship.
But actually, joy is often small.
It's a clean shirt after laundry.
It's your favorite song playing on the radio.
It's someone remembering your name.
It's the way your pet curls up beside you at night.
These are not small because they are unimportant.
They are small because they are easy to miss.
And the mind that trains itself to notice them becomes free.
The same is true with winds.
We often only celebrate the big achievements, a graduation, a promotion, a major milestone.
But life is full of quiet victories.
You answered one difficult email.
You cooked a meal instead of skipping dinner.
You studied English for 15 minutes, even when you were tired.
Each small win is like a stone on the path, alone, it looks small.
But step by step, it builds a road.
I remember one winter when I was feeling very low.
Everything felt heavy.
And I told myself, Jenny, just find one good thing each day.
Some days it was as simple as a hot cup of tea.
Other days it was a message from a friend.
And slowly, without forcing anything, my mood began to shift.
I realized the power was never in waiting for my problems to disappear.
The power was in training my eyes and heart to see what was already there.
I want you to try this too.
Even today, pick one small joy.
One simple win.
Write it down or whisper it to yourself before bed.
It could be.
I learned one new English word today.
I smiled at a stranger.
I took a deep breath when I wanted to give up.
These things count.
They always count.
Don't rush.
Good things need roots first.
This means your new habit of shifting focus won't grow in one night.
But every time you notice, a joy or honor a small win, the roots grow deeper.
And with time, they will hold you steady, even on difficult days.
So here's the reflection.
The mind clings to pain by habit.
But you can teach it to notice something else,
not by ignoring the hard parts,
but by giving equal space to the small, shining pieces of good
that are already around you.
Pause here.
Ask yourself right now.
What was one good thing that happened today?
It doesn't matter how small.
Even the smallest seed can grow into a strong tree if you keep giving it light.
Sometimes, lessons are not learned through theory.
Sometimes, they are learned through living.
I want to share a personal story with you.
It's one of those moments that taught me how dangerous negative emotions can be
and how freeing it feels to finally let them go.
A few years ago, someone said something very harsh to me.
It wasn't just criticism about my work.
It felt personal.
It felt sharp, like a knife.
I told myself, I'm fine.
I can handle it.
But the truth is, I didn't let it go.
For weeks, those words echoed in my head.
They followed me when I was walking.
They whispered while I was trying to sleep.
They showed up even when I was teaching.
The person who said it forgot about it in one day.
But I carried it for months.
One evening, I was sitting alone with a notebook.
I wrote the exact words that hurt me.
And as I looked at them on the page, something inside me broke.
I realized I was giving those words a home inside my heart.
And they did not deserve to live there.
So I did something simple.
I tore out the page.
I folded it.
And I burned it.
It wasn't magic.
The pain didn't disappear in one second.
But as the paper turned to ash, I felt a release.
My heart whispered, you don't need to keep this anymore.
That was the beginning of letting go.
Not by pretending it didn't happen.
But by deciding, this will not control me any longer.
Letting go is not always easy.
It can feel like leaving behind a part of yourself
because even pain becomes familiar.
And sometimes, we hold onto it simply
because we don't know who we are without it.
But here's the truth I learned that night.
You are not your pain.
You are not your mistakes.
You are not the words others throw at you.
You are the one who chooses whether to carry them
or to release them.
I know different cultures have their own rituals of release.
In some places, people write their worries on paper
and float them down a river.
In others, they light lanterns and watch them rise
into the night sky.
The meaning is the same everywhere.
A physical act can remind the heart to let go.
Maybe you don't have a lantern or a river.
But you have breath.
You have pen and paper.
You have the power to create your own ritual of release.
So let me ask you gently, what are you still carrying
that doesn't belong to you anymore?
Whose voice is living rent-free in your mind?
What moment are you replaying even though the world
has already moved on?
It might be time to let it go.
Here's what I realized after my own release.
When you let go, you make space.
Space for peace, space for kindness,
space for the simple joy of being alive
without that constant weight.
And strangely, the world looks softer.
Colors look brighter.
Even the silence feels kinder.
So don't be afraid to set something down,
even if it feels impossible at first.
Even if it feels scary.
Because the moment you let go of one heavy stone,
your hands are free to hold something better.
Take a breath with me now.
Inhale slowly, exhale gently.
That's the rhythm of release.
Every breath out is proof.
You already know how to let things go.
Letting go is not weakness.
It is strength in its quietest form.
And maybe, just maybe.
It's the gift you've been needing to give yourself
for a long time.
Letting go once can feel powerful,
but real transformation happens
when we choose peace, not just once,
but again and again.
Every day offers you this choice.
Do I hold on to what hurts?
Or do I practice peace, even in small ways?
Peace is not the absence of problems.
It is the presence of balance.
It is the way you decide to meet life.
You can have a noisy world outside,
but a quiet world inside.
You can have challenges on your path,
but still walk with steady steps.
Peace is not about controlling what happens.
It is about how you respond.
I think of peace like brushing your teeth.
It sounds funny, but it's true.
You don't brush your teeth once,
and then never again.
You brush them every day to protect them.
Peace works the same way.
It is not a one-time act.
It is a practice.
A small habit repeated until it becomes part of you.
So how do you choose peace every day?
You start with awareness.
Notice when your heart begins to carry heaviness.
Notice when your mind repeats old wounds.
Awareness is the door.
Then you practice release.
Take a deep breath.
Write down what hurts.
Remind yourself, I don't need to hold this today.
Finally, you turn your attention.
Look for one good thing in front of you.
It doesn't erase the problem, but it shifts the weight.
Here's something that helps me.
Every morning, before I check messages,
I pause and ask myself, what do I want to carry today?
If I carry frustration, my whole day feels sharp.
If I carry peace, my day feels lighter.
The choice is never perfect, but it is always possible.
Remember this.
Peace doesn't shout.
It whispers.
It meets you in simple moments, like drinking warm tea slowly,
like listening to the sound of rain,
like walking without rushing,
just to feel your feet on the ground.
These are not small escapes.
They are daily anchors that keep your heart steady
when the waves rise.
I know it's not always easy.
There are days when anger feels stronger than calm,
when sadness feels heavier than joy,
when the world seems determined to pull you back into negativity.
But every time you practice, even for a minute,
you are teaching your heart.
Peace is possible.
Peace is my choice.
Maybe peace for you means setting boundaries with someone.
Maybe it means turning off your phone for an hour.
Maybe it means praying, meditating,
or just sitting quietly with your breath.
There is no one formula.
Peace is personal, but the practice is universal
to choose what heals, not what hurts.
So let me leave you with this picture.
You are standing at a crossroad.
To the left is the familiar road of holding negativity.
It's crowded, noisy, and heavy.
To the right is the quieter road of peace.
It doesn't erase difficulty,
but it allows you to walk freely.
Every morning, every moment,
you stand at that crossroad again.
And every time you have the chance to choose peace.
When you practice choosing peace daily,
you don't just change how you feel.
You change how you live.
Your steps grow lighter.
Your heart grows stronger.
And the world somehow feels gentler around you
because peace is not just something you keep inside.
It becomes something you share with everyone you meet.
So tomorrow when you wake up, ask yourself softly.
What do I want to carry today?
And if your heart answers peace, listen to it.
Even if it's just for one small moment,
it will make all the difference.
Before we close today, let's slow down together.
You've walked with me through the weight of negativity,
the pull of the mind, the beauty of small joys,
the release of letting go, and the practice of peace.
It's a journey we all share, no matter where we live,
no matter what language we speak.
Take one deep breath, now, inhale, hold, exhale.
Feel the way your body softens, even just a little.
Remember, you don't need to carry every heavy emotion.
You can let some things pass.
You can shift your attention.
You can choose peace again and again.
And maybe when you practice this,
you'll also notice how your English practice feels different too
because a calm mind learns more easily.
A peaceful heart listens more deeply.
So tonight or tomorrow morning,
give yourself that gift.
One small joy, one simple win, one quiet choice of peace,
and watch how your days begin to change.
Have you experienced something like this?
Let me know in the comments.
I'd love to hear your story.
